rule: The protein route (LFQ and TMT imports on the on-disk owner, KIT-020) runs the DIA route's protein QC, normalisation, correlation, export and DA steps unchanged; its units are the DIA step map's for those steps (kit-001/step-map.json, confirmed there). The two route-specific rows are the import (protein-level readers) and the design (the LFQ/TMT branch of the design builder). No step is declared here beyond those already declared for DIA; the rows carry no flag.

units.row: each row's result depends on that row only (given the design and any declared global statistics)
units.feature_group: depends only on the rows of one feature group (the grouping column is named)
units.whole_matrix: uses a statistic or model over all rows and samples; runs once on one projected object under the cap
units.store: not a data kernel: import adoption, design, session export

steps.label: Normalisation and RUV
steps.module: R/utils_workflow_dia_products.R (runDIAReferenceNormalization; normalization-ruv declaration); KIT-129 (gate MultiScholaR.ruv_design_panel): the preset read at R/mod_prot_norm_workflow_helpers.R:497-498 (the classic table for LFQ and TMT, omicNormRuvRunTable R/mod_omic_norm_panels.R:914-919), diaNormalizationOperation("declared", supplied) by workflowRequestOperation (R/utils_workflow_operations.R:227)
steps.kernel: normaliseBetweenSamples, ruvIII_C_Varying; KIT-129 new designs: computeProtRuvModelFactors (R/func_prot_norm_optimization_helpers.R:1307-1392) with resolveRuvFactorCount and estimateRuvFactorCount (R/func_general_ruv_factor_count.R:306, :89-152), then ruvIII_C_Varying and attachProtRuvModelFactors (:1488-1502), or declareProtRuvNoFactors (:1512-1517) for a count of 0 and the design none
writes: state ruv_corrected (or normalized when RUV is skipped)

KIT-129: state ruv_corrected under every new design that ran, a count of 0 included (the normalised matrix declared without factors, config ruv_applied FALSE); normalized under the design none (the skip mode, the normalised object declaring none)

KIT-129: design_matrix W1..Wk, args$ruvCovariates (the declaration) and args$ruv_uncorrected_quant (the normalised matrix the DA tests); the product's new-design parameters and ruv_result fields as in the DIA step map's row
notes: same kernel and unit as the DIA step map's row

KIT-129 (protocol v1.11): the RUV design preset (`ruv_design`) selects groups_all_features, technical_replicates, supplied_controls, first_pass_nulls (k by ruv_k_rule) or none on the declared declaration, as on the DIA route (the DIA step map's normalisation_ruv row has the evidence); legacy is today's path. Unit unchanged (whole_matrix).

steps.label: Differential abundance
steps.module: R/utils_workflow_dia_da.R (runDIAReferenceDaAnalysis; DA-contrast-output declaration); KIT-129: diaContrastOperation(route, ruv_da_method) for a new-design source (computeDIAReferenceDaContrast R/utils_workflow_dia_da.R:474-488)
steps.kernel: differentialAbundanceAnalysis (limma); KIT-129 new designs: runProtRuvModelContrasts (R/func_prot_da_model_stats.R:437; ruvExactContrastsFit R/func_general_ruv_factor_count.R:383 with W)
writes: DA arguments committed onto correlation_filtered; contrast products
KIT-129: the contrast declaration gains ruv_da_method (ruv_factors_exact_se_trend_robust, or ruv_none_trend_robust for a count of 0 and the design none)
notes: same kernel and unit as the DIA step map's row

KIT-129 (protocol v1.11): a new-design source is tested on the uncorrected matrix with W in the model (exact standard errors), or without W on its normalised matrix; legacy is today's test on the corrected matrix (the DIA step map's da row has the evidence). Unit unchanged.
